content.title: Sebastian Fundora demolishes Keith Thurman in nasty beatdown to retain WBC super welterweight title
content.text: Sebastian Fundora staked his claim as the No. 1 fighter in the super welterweight division with an extraordinarily brutal win over former unified champion Keith Thurman. In doing so, Fundora also retained his WBC world title.It all went down at the MGM Grand Garden Arena in Las Vegas — a city where boys in boxing have become men, and where men have become legends. On Saturday, Fundora (23-1-1, 16 KOs) only added to his legend, as the 6-foot-6 154-pounder made full use of his height and reach advantages to bloody Thurman (31-2, 23 KOs) from the outside, evolving his style from an inside brawler in past bouts.AdvertisementThurman was never in the fight.Shortly after the opening bell, Fundora cracked him with a horrific left hand, buckled Thurman's knees in the second, and got after him in each and every round until his American rival's face was a bloody mess.Fundora finally, mercifully, ended things with a flurry of blows in the sixth round.In his post-fight speech, Fundora said he always used to look up to Thurman when he was watching boxing as a kid. One can only imagine what he would do to his enemies, if this was how he treated his idols.At a time in which the super welterweight division has rarely been hotter, there are numerous options for Fundora next, despite Vergil Ortiz being embroiled in a legal dispute with Golden Boy Promotions and Jaron "Boots" Ennis close to confirming a title fight against the unified champion Xander Zayas.Advertisement"Whoever wants it next," Fundora said, "they can get it."Perhaps the greatest problem for him now is that, after his bruising masterclass against Thurman, many may not voluntarily want it.Earlier in the card, Yoenis Tellez (12-1, 8 KOs) overcame a nasty head-butt and possibly broken nose to convincingly outpoint Brian Mendoza (23-5, 17 KOs) in the co-main event, and Gurgen Hovhannisyan (10-0, 9 KOs) beat Cesar Navarro (15-4, 13 KOs) in the fifth round.Perhaps the most impressive performance on the undercard, though, came from Yoenli Hernandez (10-0, 9 KOs), who finished Terrell Gausha (24-6, 12 KOs) with a disputed stoppage in the fourth round but otherwise looked like a force at middleweight. And considering how wide open the 160-pound division is, a world title could be his for the taking, off the back of the skill set he showed on Prime Video PPV.AdvertisementCheck out full Fundora vs. Thurman results and highlights below, as well as Uncrowned's play-by-play of the main card.Main cardWBC super welterweight championship: Sebastian Fundora def.
